cf.title: CREATE TABLE .. LIKE copies comments to an unrelated table

input.subject: CREATE TABLE .. LIKE copies comments to an unrelated table

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The thread states the bug with a reproducible case, four people reproduced or tested it, and the fix extends the schema qualification that permanent tables already get. The remaining points are backpatch scope and a check of other generated commands, which a committer can settle during code review.

brief.title: Fix create temp table like copying comments to another table
brief.problem: With pg_temp listed after another schema in search_path, create temp table ... (like src including comments) applies the copied comments to a same-named table in the earlier schema. It overwrites that table's column comment, or fails with "constraint ... does not exist". Any user who puts pg_temp late in search_path is affected.
brief.proposed_design: transformCreateStmt() already schema-qualifies the target name for permanent tables so that the commands generated after creation find the right table. The patch qualifies temp table names too, using the actual temp schema name (pg_temp_N), so the generated CommentStmts no longer depend on search_path.
user_visible_surface: Behaviour change: copied comments now land on the new temp table, and the command no longer fails when the other table lacks a matching constraint.
author_claims: The CommentStmts from like ... including comments name the table by a name list, which loses relpersistence.
The fix applies to both column and constraint comments.
The patch targets stable branches as a bug fix.
brief.thread_state: Junwang Zhao, Koshi Shibagaki, Salma El-Sayed and João Rito reviewed or tested; v2 adds the constraint test Salma asked for. Koshi raised a concurrent temp schema rename that now errors; he and Jim agreed it needs no handling because it requires a superuser.
unclear: The patch does not say whether other commands generated by transformCreateStmt(), besides comments, had the same exposure.
No one has checked the other callers of transformCreateStmt().
The thread does not say which stable branches the fix should go to.
search_queries: schema qualified name temp table generated commands

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: ProcessUtility hooks and event triggers may now see generated subcommands that name pg_temp_N instead of an unqualified temp table name.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The patch changes which table a generated COMMENT resolves to when search_path lists another schema before pg_temp.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry targets stable branches, and the fix changes behaviour of create temp table ... like in released versions.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which stable branches should receive the fix, and does the patch apply and pass the new tests on each of them?
Do other commands generated by transformCreateStmt(), besides the CommentStmts, look up the temp table by name and so had the same exposure?
Do the other callers of transformCreateStmt() behave the same once temp table names are schema-qualified?
Do error messages or event trigger output for create temp table now show pg_temp_N where they showed an unqualified name before?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows parse_utilcmd.c and the namespace lookup rules for temp schemas would have to own it; the visible thread shows reviewers and testers but no one identified as a committer.
committability.liability: A behaviour change in transformCreateStmt() on stable branches: the owner signs for every generated subcommand of create temp table now carrying the pg_temp_N schema name, for the life of each back branch.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v1 in message #4 and v2 in message #9 with the constraint test a reviewer asked for, which shows active follow-up within the thread.

priority.reason: The bug needs pg_temp listed after a schema holding a same-named table, so few users hit it, but the result is a silent overwrite of another table's comment. The patch is about 6 KiB, touches one backend file plus regression tests, and adds no new surface.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so three points are unchecked: whether other generated commands had the same exposure, how the other callers of transformCreateStmt() behave, and whether the fix applies cleanly to each stable branch.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Temporary tables that do not bloat pg_catalog (a.k.a fast temp tables)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch added a new kind of temporary table (CREATE FAST TEMP TABLE) whose catalog information is kept in the creating backend's memory instead of in pg_catalog. The goal was to avoid pg_catalog bloat and the autovacuum work caused by applications that create and drop many temporary tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas objected that if the catalog entries live only in backend-private memory, other sessions cannot see the dependencies, so objects the temporary table depends on (for example functions used in indexes, triggers or defaults) can be dropped by other backends. Without globally visible dependency entries the design was not seen as workable. He also objected that the patch adds an in-memory heap implementation inside low-level heapam code paths instead of using a proper storage API, which he considered not maintainable. Alternative designs discussed later in the thread were judged to address the bloat problem only partly.
matched_queries: schema qualified name temp table generated commands
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Until we've got a
strategy for that problem, this whole effort is going nowhere - even
though in other respects it may be a terrific idea.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent extension creation in temporary schemas
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch first made create extension fail when the target schema is a temporary schema, as alter extension set schema already does. After objections, the author dropped that and changed psql's \dx and \dx+ to hide extensions in other sessions' temporary schemas.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Chris Travers objected that other objects such as types can already be created in temporary schemas, so blocking extensions only would add another special case. The author dropped the block and kept only the \dx and \dx+ fix, which Chris Travers marked Ready for Committer. The author then found that a second session cannot create an extension already created in another session's temporary schema, but \dx no longer lists it. He returned the patch because it does not solve the root problem and makes things more confusing.
matched_queries: schema qualified name temp table generated commands
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The patch as it stands does not actually solve the root problem and
makes things a bit confusing, so I am marking it as returned with
feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add CREATE SCHEMA ... LIKE support
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds `CREATE SCHEMA <name> LIKE <source_schema>` with `INCLUDING | EXCLUDING` options, which copies the objects of a source schema into a new schema. The first version covered tables and indexes; later versions added foreign keys and partitions, with warnings when an object references another schema.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Álvaro Herrera questioned adding DDL syntax for this at all, given the many hard cases and the extra clauses proposed for CREATE SCHEMA. He suggested building on the DDL-generating functions proposed in other threads. The author agreed that a function such as pg_get_schema_ddl() seemed a better way. The visible messages do not show a later version or an explicit closing decision.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This whole thing seems like a giant can of worms, and I'm not sure it's
a good idea to add DDL syntax for it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow excluding pg_temp or pg_catalog from search_path.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds special search_path entries "!pg_temp" and "!pg_catalog" that stop Postgres from searching pg_temp or pg_catalog implicitly, as a safety option for functions. It also warns when a user creates a schema with one of these special names, such as "$user".
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author doubted the feature's value without his separate SEARCH clause proposal, which did not gain support, because users would have to type "!pg_temp" by hand and pg_temp is already ignored for function and operator lookup. The reviewer agreed it was not worth adding without that main use case, and the author withdrew the entry. Earlier review comments also noted that the names need quoting and that "!pg_temp" is ignored when pg_temp is listed explicitly.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I thought it sounded generally useful, but if we're not going to proceed
with the primary use-case for this feature, then perhaps it's not worth
going through this particular one-way door at this time.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_get_constraintdef: Schema qualify foreign tables unless pretty printing is enabled
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_get_constraintdef schema-qualify the referenced table in a foreign key's REFERENCES clause when pretty printing is off, as pg_get_indexdef already does. The goal is constraint definitions that can be recreated on another system with a different search_path.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said pg_get_indexdef is the odd one out, since most generate_relation_name calls in ruleutils.c ignore the pretty flag, and Alvaro Herrera judged the patch too small for making PRETTYFLAG_SCHEMA work consistently. Tom asked for a clearly defined rule on which call sites qualify names, with a documented helper function. The author did not reply to these reviews, and Michael Paquier returned the patch after six weeks without a reply.
matched_queries: schema qualified name temp table generated commands
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In other words, I think your patch is too small.

precedents_retrieved.title: Global temporary table
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add global temporary tables to PostgreSQL: a table definition stored once in the catalog, with each session getting its own private data files, local buffers, statistics and relfrozenxid tracking, kept in session-local hash tables plus a shared-memory hash that tracks which backends use each table. DDL on such a table would be allowed only when no other session holds data in it, and operations that change the relfilenode (VACUUM FULL, CLUSTER) would be disabled.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund held that the patch could not be merged with anything close to its current design, calling it unmaintainable, and said fundamental design work was needed first, possibly through a generic way to split catalog tables into local and non-local storage. Robert Haas found the patch too big and unpolished to review: one large code drop with weak comments and code quality, where reviewers kept finding crash bugs. He asked that it be split into independently committable patches and said reaching a committable state may require a near-total rewrite. Given these two opinions that it could not be reviewed effectively as it stood, the entry was marked Returned with Feedback.

I think there's just no way that it can be merged with anything close to the

precedents_retrieved.title: create table like: ACCESS METHOD
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Michael Paquier, Vik Fearing
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an ACCESS METHOD option to CREATE TABLE ... LIKE, so that INCLUDING ACCESS METHOD (and INCLUDING ALL) copies the source table's table access method to the new table. Partitioned tables would silently ignore the option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: LIKE expands to column definitions, but the access method is a table property, so two LIKE clauses with different access methods can conflict. Its interaction with USING is also undefined. The patch overwrote any AM given in USING, and Michael Paquier asked for a clear definition of these corner cases. Peter Eisentraut argued that this syntax is the wrong approach and suggested something like USING (LIKE t1).
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Whereas the access method is a table property.  So I don't think this syntax is the right approach for this feature.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix search_path for maintenance commands
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch sets search_path to "pg_catalog, pg_temp" while ANALYZE, CLUSTER, REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, REINDEX, VACUUM and CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW run as the table owner. This makes the commands behave the same for every caller and keeps a role with the MAINTAIN privilege from using search_path to gain the table owner's privileges.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Jeff Davis withdrew the patch after a reviewer reported that it no longer applied to HEAD, saying it was not yet clear this was the right change. He had already noted that it forces search_path in maintenance commands but not in other contexts, and that his broader proposals to fix search_path for functions got little agreement. Earlier concerns about breaking functions that depend on search_path were raised in messages not shown. Nathan Bossart supported committing it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I am withdrawing this patch from the CF until it's more clear that this is what we really want to do.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 3a60c8ff892a8242b907f44702bfd9f1ff877d45.  Buildfarm
results show that that caused a whole bunch of new warnings on platforms
where gcc believes the local printf to be non-POSIX-compliant.  This
problem outweighs the hypothetical-anyway possibility of getting warnings
for misuse of %m.  We could use gnu_printf archetype when we've substituted
src/port/snprintf.c, but that brings us right back to the problem of not
getting warnings for %m.

A possible answer is to attack it in the other direction by insisting
that %m support be included in printf's feature set, but that will take
more investigation.  In the meantime, revert the previous change, and
update the comment for PGAC_C_PRINTF_ARCHETYPE to more fully explain
what's going on.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P21] was reverted over repeated name lookups in partition commands, and [P6] was returned over inconsistent schema qualification in ruleutils.c output; neither recorded reason applies to this bug fix. This patch removes a search_path-dependent lookup and extends the qualification that permanent tables already get. The thread cites no earlier discussion of this bug, and the stale-name concern from message #5 was settled in messages #6 and #7.

No standards or compatibility objection from this angle. The patch adds no syntax, keyword, GUC or catalog object, and pg_dump does not dump temp tables, so there is no round-trip concern. The only user-visible change is that copied comments land on the new temp table instead of an unrelated one, which is the bug fix itself; the thread shows no user who depends on the old result. The concurrent temp schema rename was settled in messages #6 and #7, since it requires a superuser and permanent tables already behave the same way. Not checked without the code: whether other statements generated by transformCreateStmt() now show pg_temp_N in error messages or event trigger output. A committer would likely ask which stable branches the fix targets, but that is a backpatch scoping question, not an objection.

From the replication and on-disk angle there is nothing to object to. The patch only changes how transformCreateStmt() names the temp table in the commands it generates, so it has no on-disk format, WAL, catalog, catversion or wire protocol change and nothing new for pg_upgrade or pg_dump. Temp tables are not replicated physically or logically. One point I could not check without the code: ProcessUtility hooks now see subcommands that name pg_temp_N directly, which could matter to extensions that capture DDL, but temp tables are rarely captured that way.

The patch closes an exposure and opens none. Generated COMMENT commands now name the temp table by its real schema, so a same-named table earlier in search_path no longer receives them. COMMENT still checks ownership. Before the patch, the misdirected comment could land only on a table the caller owns, so this is not privilege escalation. No unprivileged user can create or rename a pg_temp_N schema, because the pg_ prefix is reserved and renaming needs a superuser. That leaves the stale-name window from message #5, which the thread settled in messages #6 and #7. The repeated name lookup in [P21] does not fit here, since an attacker would need superuser rights to swap the target. No new privilege, default, information leak or resource use appears. Not checked, because the code is not shown: whether other commands generated by transformCreateStmt() resolve the table by OID or by name.

No objection holds from the maintenance angle. This is a one-line bug fix in transformCreateStmt() that extends the existing schema qualification of permanent tables to temp tables. It adds no GUC, no catalog change, no API and no cost on a common path, and because it acts where all later generated commands get their target name, future LIKE options also benefit. The concurrent temp schema rename case was raised in message #5 and settled in messages #6 and #7. [P21] concerns repeated name lookups, but this patch follows the existing practice for permanent tables, and replacing name lookups with OIDs would be a separate, larger change that does not belong in a stable-branch fix. What cannot be checked without the code: whether other generated statements had the same exposure, and which branches the fix applies to cleanly.

This is a bug fix: comments get written to an unrelated table, or the command fails. Writing `create temp table pg_temp.foo (...)` or putting pg_temp first in search_path avoids it, but users cannot know they need to, and no extension or existing feature can stand in for a fix to the wrong-target write.

This is a bug fix for silent data corruption: copied comments overwrite another table's comments, or the command fails. Demand objections do not apply to bug fixes. The cost falls only on the temp-table path, and four people reproduced the bug or tested the fix (messages #2, #5, #8, #10).
